title: Each accepted connection reaches one operator, once
body: The software shall carry the file descriptor of each connection the platform's listener accepts to exactly one operator thread, each descriptor delivered once and in the order the listener handed it over.
rationale: kyr_host's listener accepts and hands each socket to the least loaded operator, which then serves it alone: a lost descriptor is a client left hanging, a duplicate is one socket served twice.
criteria: Descriptors handed over by one thread to another arrive once each, in order, none lost, under load and under the thread sanitizer.

title: The listener never waits on an operator
body: Handing a descriptor over shall never block, sleep, spin or take a lock: when the operator cannot take it the hand-off shall refuse at once, so that the listener answers the client from a reject slot and goes on accepting.
rationale: The listener is one thread for the whole box; a hand-off that waits on one slow operator stalls every new connection.
criteria: A hand-off on a full ring returns a refusal in a bounded number of steps; no lock or system call is on the hand-off's path.

title: A bounded ring, sized once
body: Each operator's ring shall hold a number of descriptors fixed when the operator starts, any power of two from 8 to 1024 (KYR_HOST_RING_CAPACITY, 32 by default), every slot of it usable.
rationale: The platform sizes each operator's mailbox once at boot, as its allocation style asks; a slot lost to the empty-or-full ambiguity would be a connection refused for nothing.
criteria: A ring of each capacity from 8 to 1024 takes exactly that many descriptors before it refuses one.

title: The operator drains without waiting
body: On its wake-up the operator shall take every descriptor handed over before it, one at a time, each take answering at once whether there was one, until none is left.
rationale: The operator's thread runs its reactor; a take that blocked would stop every client it serves.
criteria: Taking from an empty ring answers 'none' at once; a drain after N hand-offs takes N descriptors.

title: One ring per operator for the process's life
body: A ring shall be created by its operator's start, refuse the start when it cannot be made, serve the operator for the whole life of the process (months of uptime at the connection rate of a box) and be released by its teardown.
rationale: The operator owns its mailbox; a box restarts rarely, so nothing in the ring may wear out with the number of connections.
criteria: A failed creation is reported to the caller; the indexes do not wrap in any realistic uptime; the teardown frees everything.

title: Delivered as the platform pins its libraries
body: The software shall be delivered as the Debian packages libspscring and libspscring-dev, tier 1 of the platform (no platform dependency of its own), built reproducibly and pinned by the platform by version and SHA-256 in deps.txt.
rationale: Every platform library is resolved from deps.txt; a tier 1 library sits under every other.
criteria: The packages install and a program built against them alone runs; two builds give the same bytes; the pins resolve.

title: Qualified under the platform's build profiles
body: Each release the platform pins shall be built and tested under the platform's kyr-build profiles (release, sanitizers, thread sanitizer, coverage), its pipeline green at the release commit.
rationale: The ring is concurrent code inside the box's front door; the platform takes no release whose concurrent paths have not run under the thread sanitizer.
criteria: The release pipeline's run at the release commit is recorded, every stage passed.

title: A C interface of create, push, pop and destroy
body: The supplier shall provide a C11 header declaring an opaque ring type and the calls to create a ring of a given capacity, push an int, pop an int into the caller's variable and destroy the ring, setting the caller's pointer to NULL.
rationale: These are the four calls kyr_host makes (operator.c and worker.c); the type is held by pointer in operator_t.
criteria: The header compiles in a C11 consumer; the four calls exist with these shapes.

title: Statuses as return values
body: Push and pop shall return 0 on success and -1 when the ring is full or empty (or not there), with no other effect on a refusal and no errno to read.
rationale: kyr_host tests the return against 0 and nothing else.
criteria: Each refusal returns -1 and leaves the ring and the caller's variable as they were.

title: One pushing thread, one popping thread, no lock
body: Push shall be safe from exactly one thread and pop from exactly one other thread at the same time, with no lock on either side; creation and destruction happen while neither uses the ring.
rationale: The listener's thread is the one producer of every ring and each operator's thread its one consumer.
criteria: Under the thread sanitizer, one producer and one consumer run without a reported race.

title: The value popped is the value pushed
body: A descriptor popped shall be exactly the one pushed, visible in full to the popping thread: the hand-off shall order the producer's write of the value before the consumer's read of it.
rationale: A torn or stale descriptor routes one client's socket to another's state.
criteria: An inspection of the memory ordering; the threaded suites deliver every value intact.

title: Linkage: versioned shared object and archive
body: The library shall be a shared object with a versioned soname and versioned symbols, exporting exactly its declared functions, and a static archive with the same functions.
rationale: kyr_host links the shared object in its tests and the box's servers link it at run time; a consumer built against another major must fail at load, not at run time.
criteria: The soname, the version node and the exports match the header.
